headline: Deep learning models for variant effect and genome annotation across species
label: Deep Learning Genomic Variant Prediction
summary: Genome-scale benchmarks now test variant pathogenicity and splice-altering predictors across human and non-human species.
synthesis: Across this set, the dominant thread is deep learning applied to genomic variant interpretation and sequence analysis. AnnotateMissense benchmarks missense pathogenicity predictors over 90.6M hg38 variants by integrating dbNSFP, AlphaMissense and ESM features. MOSAIC fuses a DNA language model, multi-scale CNN and annotation features for noncanonical splice-altering variants, and NCBoost v2 classifies non-coding SNVs in Mendelian disease. MuRaL-indel applies a U-Net to base-resolution INDEL mutation rate maps. A multi-species review reports that task-specific models and genomic foundation models lose roughly 21–33% AUROC across human, rat, pig and chicken, while Porcine MutBERT offers 86M-parameter lightweight models. Other items extend the theme to long-read structural variant calling (gSV), DNA language model embeddings for metagenomic binning (DCVBin), and learned residue-level scoring for alignment (BABAPPAlign).
